CARD. Rosa M. Navarrete (DOB 1974-03-27, MRN RB44615037, preferred language Spanish) holds an approved Medical Hardship award (applied 2024-11-14, household percent 487.3 = 99600.00 / 20440.00 on the 2024 guideline, determined 2024-12-12, award 2023-11-15 to 2025-12-12, cap 9960.00 = 10.0 percent of income under the base cap because it was determined before the cap schedule's 2025-10-01 effective date). The renewal reminder went out 2025-11-12; she filed the renewal through the portal on 2025-11-14 (inside the 30-day window). The renewal case carries the award's household size 2, income 99600.00 and liquid assets 14300.00, the household percent recomputed on the 2025 guideline in force on its application date (99600.00 / 21150.00 = 470.9, still Medical Hardship), no claimed medical debt (0.00), and only her BadgerCare Plus determination notice (accepted 2025-11-17). She asks for the list of papers and the deadline. Root: assist_ext_response_window (155 response days). Its prerequisite sentence (state form) waits on the renewal case recording the medical debt the renewal claims, which only her signed claim writes (assist_ext_renewal_debt_claim, owner=user, 6018.58). Draw: 1 prerequisite problem, factor counts [6, 4].

GOLD WRITE ORDER: sign_renewal_debt_claim_3b9e07c1 (user, 6018.58 on the renewal case) -> send_missing_information_notice_7f5665e5 (155 days, Spanish, INCOME/RESIDENCY/OUTSIDE BILLS/BANK STATEMENT all REQUESTED, MEDICAID notice NOT_REQUESTED; due 2026-04-22). Skipping the claim leaves 0.00, below a quarter of the hardship share (4980.00): outside-bills days 21, response days 161 (due 2026-04-28).

BASE CLAUSES CHECKED UN-IGNITED: no account in bad_debt or past a final notice (three statemented accounts are on the Assistance-Linked plan, which stops final notices; the CT account is on an itemization-review hold placed 2025-11-13 before any statement; the MRI account was put on a GFE-dispute hold 2025-09-29, before any statement, under the estimate charter's dispute hold); the award is applied to the three accounts whose insured patient responsibility posted (insured charge basis = posted responsibility: 2212.40, 3236.50 and the re-priced CT 367.84 on its 2025-11-13 application row, 5816.74 of the 9960.00 cap used, no adjustment, no refund review); the elective MRI and the elective May 14 clinic visit are outside the award (elective_excluded); the November ED account awaits adjudication; the plan is current: installments 1-7 paid through 2025-10-15, and the 2025-11-15 installment fell due after the renewal was filed (submitted 2025-11-14), so it is paused under the plan charter (fap_pending_pause_days 90) and not drawn; renewal reminder logged; no notice on the renewal other than the root.

SEED (re-priced in rounds 2 and 4; every cross-category row is listed with its owning-charter check in the worklog table): ED claim (Network Health) allowed 3062.00 = deductible 2000.00 + coinsurance 212.40 + paid 849.60, contractual 1818.00; surgery claim (Quartz) allowed 6182.50 = deductible 2500.00 + coinsurance 736.50 + paid 2946.00, contractual 8677.50; the allowed amount falls 1544.70 (20.0%) short of Quartz's expected 52.0% of charges (7727.20), so Riverbend filed an underpayment appeal on 2025-09-24 (inside the 90-day provider window), still within the payer's 60-day decision time on the notice date (appealed); October CT claim (Quartz) allowed at the expected 1539.20 = copay 75.00 + coinsurance 292.84 (20% of allowed less copay) + paid 1171.36, contractual 1420.80. May 14 clinic visit (elective, coverage gap) denied PR-27 by Network Health on 2025-06-13 (27 days after billing, inside the 30 clean-claim days) and posted COVERAGE_TERMINATED 1180.00, first statement 2025-06-17; its financial class corrected to SELF_PAY (encounter/claim charters), no uninsured discount (final bill dropped to the payer). September cervical-spine MRI (72141, a code not on the imaging package schedule, so a single-service GFE is the type): Quartz denied prior authorization, the patient elected self-pay; single-service GFE issued 2025-09-04 (convening facility 1800.00 = total), billed 3120.00 less the 25 percent elective imaging discount 780.00 = 2340.00, exceeding the estimate by 540.00 (>= 400.00), dispute filed 2025-09-29 within 120 days of the 2025-09-26 initial bill. Plan: 2212.40 / 48 = 46.09; add-ons recomputed over 48 less installments paid (3018.13 / 45 = 67.07; 6187.56 / 44 = 140.63), applied oldest service first (ED account, balance 1585.17); balance 5765.67. Coverage-terminated discounts posted under the published encounter rules on the day of each PR-27 release, before any statement (so no service-recovery courtesy is owed): May 14 visit, elective clinic 20 percent of 1180.00 = 236.00 (no allowance), balance 944.00, enrolled on the plan 2025-07-01 at 944.00; October 28 visit, clinic 40 percent plus 2.5 points for one other PR-27 release (the May 14 claim) = 42.5 percent of 830.00 = 352.75, balance 477.25. No encounter write is owed at the opening.

FACTOR CARD.
- Renewal claim (standard 9577.99, result 6018.58): renewal_appeal_holdout P [underpayment appeal, appealed -> coinsurance 736.50 off]; renewal_hold_holdout M [itemization-review hold -> coinsurance 292.84 off]; renewal_coverage_gap P [coverage-gap account = the October 28 clinic visit (most recent coverage-terminated liability, 2025-11-17), medically necessary, notice on the renewal case -> balance 477.25 net of its 352.75 discount, 190.07 above the AGB share 287.18 off; the elective May 14 visit's balance stands as posted]; renewal_gfe_dispute P [estimate in dispute -> billed 2340.00 off].
- Response window (standard 30, result 155): period_reach M [latest first statement 2025-07-12, 129 days -> MX(30, 111) = 111]; outside_bills_days P [no outside bills received, claim between 4980.00 and 19920.00 -> 15]; pending_claim_days P [accepted ED claim -> 5]; treatment_days P [service 9 days back -> 14]; appeal_days P [underpayment appeal (other type) -> 5]; account_count_days P [3 first statements -> 5].
Multi-source: renewal_appeal_holdout, renewal_coverage_gap, renewal_gfe_dispute, outside_bills_days, appeal_days. Cross-difficulty: encounter, claim, estimate.

C14 METHOD SHAPE — all-pairs tier tables.
renewal_hold_holdout (hold_out): T1 = MN(disputed line charge, held liabilities) (min-pick); T2 = held account's coinsurance (windowed sum); T3 = 0.
  T1 vs T2: a charge-dispute account with a disputed line 300.00 and coinsurance 292.84 among liabilities 367.84: MN(300.00, 367.84) = 300.00 vs 292.84.  T1 vs T3: any disputed line (300.00 vs 0).  T2 vs T3: this world 292.84 vs 0.
period_reach (base_part): T1 = (application_period_days - age) + missing_information_response_days (countdown plus the standard window); T2 = MX(missing_information_response_days, application_period_days - age) (floored countdown); T3 = missing_information_response_days (constant).
  T1 vs T2: on T1's own domain they differ by 30 (age 100: 170 vs 140); across the boundary age 120 gives 150, age 121 gives 119.  T1 vs T3: any age up to 120 (age 49: 221 vs 30).  T2 vs T3: this world 111 vs 30.

Decoys leave both values unchanged; XLATEST ties keep the first row; absent records fall through without exception (no first statement -> base 30 and no account days = 69). Edges follow the rule words: a statement exactly 120 days old is in tier 1, 121 days in tier 2; a REQUESTED outside-bills row is not a receipt; a claim of exactly 4980.00 is "at least" a quarter of the share; a service exactly 14 days back is "near", 15 days falls to 7. No division in either computation.

REALISM. IRS 501(r): 240-day application period from the first post-discharge statement, 120-day notification period, missing-information notice with a completion window, AGB (agb_pct 34.6); HHS guideline in force on each application date (2024: 20440.00, 2025: 21150.00 for two). No Surprises Act patient-provider dispute ($400, 120 days, collection hold while pending). Response-day, claim and outside-bills ladders are Riverbend's own published FAP schedules; no tenure tiers, no invented statute.

The expiring award's last application ran 2025-11-13 (three days after the CT remittance), so this account carries no award application yet; it has no first statement yet, and its date of service is older than the November ED visit (registered on the new Security Health Plan card, member SH44620934, billed 2025-11-13 and accepted; persona's 'same jobs' holds: the employer changed carriers, not the jobs), so the response window's statement, treatment, appeal and pending-claim inputs are unchanged. The factor bears weight through a denial inside the payer's decision time (round-3 dating of a May visit denied on day 196 removed). Gold: renewal claim 6018.58 after the round-10 coverage-terminated discounts (6254.58 before), response days 155 unchanged; the skip run still gives 161.
user_scenario:
You are Rosa M. Navarrete, 51, calling Riverbend Regional Health's Patient Financial Services on your lunch break from the dental office in Appleton where you work at the front desk. You are friendly and organized, and you have the letter Riverbend mailed you last week on the table in front of you. Last year Riverbend approved you for financial help after a car accident left you with big hospital bills, and the letter says that help ends on December 12. After the letter came you filled in the renewal form in the Riverbend patient portal last Friday, but nobody has told you what papers to send. What you want from this call is for Riverbend to send you the list of papers you need to provide so the help can keep going after that, and to know the deadline for sending them.

You start by saying that you got a letter saying your financial help from Riverbend ends on December 12, and that you would like them to send you the list of papers you need to give them to keep the help going, with the deadline. You do not offer account numbers or amounts on your own.

When you are asked who you are, you give your name, Rosa M. Navarrete, and your date of birth, March 27, 1974, which you also read out as 1974-03-27 if they want it in that form. If they need one more detail, you read your medical record number off the letter: RB44615037. Only if they ask for something else do you add that your phone number is 9205550461, your ZIP code is 54911, and the last four of your Social Security number are 4836.

If the representative asks whether anything has changed since last year, you say nothing has: it is still just you and your husband Luis, you both have the same jobs and the same pay, and your savings are about the same. If they ask about bills from doctors or hospitals outside Riverbend, you say you still owe the Milwaukee hospital where you had surgery after the accident and you have those bills at home, but you have not sent anything to Riverbend this year. If they ask you for income, savings or debt figures, you say you would rather they use what Riverbend already has on file from last year.

If the representative explains that something has to be signed by you yourself and offers to put it in your patient portal, you say that is fine; once they hand it to you, you sign it as they have set it up, and if they ask, you read back what the confirmation on your screen says. If they ask whether they may go ahead from their side, you tell them yes.

When the representative tells you the list has been sent and gives you the deadline, you repeat the deadline back once to make sure you have it right, thank them and say goodbye. If they tell you instead that it cannot be done today, you ask once what happens next, listen, and end the call politely. You do not ask for anything else during the call.
